title: MemoryTax: The Bitter Lesson of Agent Memory
abstract: arXiv:2610.29823v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agent memory systems such as Mem0 and Zep decide what to keep before any question arrives; coding agents keep the raw history and let the model search it with its own tools. We ask whether designed memory still helps once the model is strong enough to search for itself. On one LoCoMo conversation (419 turns, 152 questions), we run four memory methods (full context, BM25, Mem0, Zep) and three coding agents (Pi, Codex, Claude Code), each with GPT-4o-mini, GPT-6 Luna and Claude Opus 5.5, and record what every rollout costs. This is a short empirical study, with one conversation and one run per cell. Agent memory is a costly patch for a weak model: Mem0 beats full context only with GPT-4o-mini, and its build alone costs more than a whole full-context rollout. Agent memory also has a ceiling, set by the model that writes it: a stronger reader does not recover what a weaker writer left out. With Claude Opus 5.5, Pi tops the cost-accuracy front

translated_title: MemoryTax：智能体记忆的苦涩教训
translated_abstract: 诸如 Mem0 和 Zep 等智能体记忆系统在任何问题到来之前就预先决定保留哪些内容；而编程智能体（coding agents）则保留原始历史记录，让模型用自身工具去搜索它。我们探究当模型足够强大、能够自主检索时，精心设计的记忆机制是否仍有帮助。在一个 LoCoMo 对话（419 轮，152 个问题）上，我们运行了四种记忆方法（全上下文、BM25、Mem0、Zep）和三个编程智能体（Pi、Codex、Claude Code），每种配置分别搭配 GPT-4o-mini、GPT-6 Luna 和 Claude Opus 5.5，并记录每次运行的成本。这是一项简短的实证研究，每个实验单元仅使用一个对话和一次运行。研究表明，智能体记忆对弱模型而言是一种昂贵的补丁：Mem0 仅在使用 GPT-4o-mini 时才胜过全上下文方法，且其构建成本本身就超过了一次完整的全上下文运行。智能体记忆还存在一个由写入模型决定的上限：更强的读取者无法挽回更弱的写入者所遗漏的信息。在使用 Claude Opus 5.5 时，Pi 在成本-精度前沿上表现最佳。
tldr: 这项实证研究揭示了智能体记忆的“苦涩教训”——精心设计的记忆系统只是弱模型的昂贵补丁（仅对 GPT-4o-mini 有用且构建成本高昂），其效果受写入模型能力封顶，而强模型直接搜索原始历史的全上下文方式在成本-精度上更优。
en_tdlr: This empirical study reveals the bitter lesson of agent memory: designed memory systems are merely a costly patch for weak models—useful only for GPT-4o-mini with build costs exceeding full-context rollouts, capped by the writing model's ability, while strong models like Claude Opus 5.5 achieve better cost-accuracy tradeoffs by directly searching raw history with Pi.
